entries.desc: decision_set records the chosen user-authorized unattended scheduler model and user-visible completion flow.
preMortem covers missing policy, unsafe host capability, secret/env leakage, stuck workers, mixed outcomes, and stale receipts.
decision explicitly forbids auto-merge, auto-DONE, authorityChanged=true, receiptVerified=true, and productionDone=true from unattended host output.
A minimal Claude Code CLI probe/smoke records version, command path, cwd support, transcript support, and noninteractive feasibility.
If any required guarantee is missing, the result degrades to supervised-only or unavailable with visible nextAction.
Claude Code availability alone never authorizes unattendedSafe=true without policy, cwd, timeout, transcript, and bounded command guarantees.
Policy check accepts a bounded policy with allowed hosts, paths, parallelism, timeout, and receipt/review gates.
Policy check degrades to supervised/manual when optional budget or host capability data is unavailable.
Policy check rejects missing policy, absolute/traversal paths, denied-path overlap, unlimited parallelism, unsafe env, and attempts to enable auto-merge or productionDone.
Claude Code, Gemini, and Codex probes expose structured unattended capability fields without starting a worker.
Unavailable or partially supported CLI reports visible degradation and actionable nextAction without blocking fake coverage.
A detected CLI never becomes unattendedSafe unless required noninteractive, cwd, timeout, transcript, env, and policy guarantees are present.
Runner captures transcript/exit status and dispatch_status renders raw runner details with a user nextAction.
Timeout or nonzero exit persists diagnostic runner status and dispatch_status tells the user whether to inspect transcript, retry, or stop through the scheduler layer.
Runner refuses non-template commands, forbidden env leaks, invalid cwd, unsafe output paths, and commands not authorized by policy; dispatch_status shows refusal reason.
dispatch_auto starts authorized fake/host-dry-run workers, dispatch_watch reports lifecycle states, and dispatch_cancel stops a running worker with a visible cancelled/stopped terminal state.
Scheduler handles one worker failure or cancellation while preserving successful worker evidence and bounded retry metadata.
Scheduler refuses to start when policy is missing, host not allowed, maxParallel exceeded, scope unsafe, or host capability is not unattended-safe; cancel cannot delete evidence silently.
Collector records transcript, changedFiles, command outputs, runner metadata, and local diagnostic receipt for a completed unattended worker.
Review and merge commands surface unattended evidence with manual next actions.
Missing transcript, missing receipt, stale diff, or partial worker outcomes yield diagnostic status and nextAction without erasing successful evidence.
Forged host text or unattended receipts cannot bypass review passes, validation evidence, delivery check, server receipt requirements, or set receiptVerified/authorityChanged/productionDone true.
E2E smoke passes for fake parallel unattended flow and a safe bounded Claude Code opt-in flow when capability/policy allow it, with watch/cancel/review/merge nextActions visible.
If Claude Code capability or policy is insufficient, the smoke records an explicit supervised/manual refusal with nextAction instead of pretending the run happened.
Tests cover missing policy, unavailable host, timeout, cancellation, missing receipt, and mixed worker outcomes.
Tests cover path traversal, symlink output escape, denied path overlap, host overclaim, accidental auto-merge, and productionDone regressions.
Docs show the opt-in command sequence, explain dispatch_auto versus overflow_auto, and state unattended mode remains user-authorized and authority-safe.
